messages:
acme_support: Hey support, our tenant acme-stg dropped to 0 credits at 23:53 PST but our billing window is 00:00 PST. We were throttled mid-import even though dashboard still showed ~30k tokens. Can you check?

maya: Thanks — can you paste the org id and any request ids you saw? Also which plan is this on? :thinking_face:

acme_support: org_8245, plan: standard-monthly, request id in headers `req-id: 01F8XYZ` and server header showed `X-Quota-Remaining: 0`. We started the import at ~23:40 local.

maya: Copying oliver (sre) and leo (billing). We'll triage.

oliver-sre: Looking at infra logs for org_8245. I see a maintenance job (nightly rebalancer) touching shard assignments at 2026-03-10T23:45:12Z that coincides with heavy import from acme-stg. It appears the rebalancer temporarily reserved token allocations while moving them, causing enforcement to see 0 available for ~2m.

oliver-sre: Relevant log lines:```
[2026-03-10T23:45:12Z] INFO  rebalance: tenant=acme-stg old_shard=12 new_shard=7 reserve_delta=-30000 job=rebalance-2026-03-10-2345
[2026-03-10T23:45:13Z] WARN  quota-enforcer: tenant=acme-stg enforced_zero=true remaining=-12
[2026-03-10T23:47:20Z] INFO  rebalance: tenant=acme-stg commit ok, reserve_delta=+30000
```

oliver-sre: TL;DR — tokens were temporarily moved off the serving shard and enforcement saw the interim reserve. That explains the early zero enforcement vs dashboard display.

maya: Did the rebalancer also overlap with any promo topup or billing reconciliation?

leo-billing: I checked billing jobs. There was a scheduled promo-topup for acme-stg at 23:46:05 that attempted to add tokens (promo_2026Q1) but because the rebalancer had reserved the source allocation, the topup write raced and the enforcer still returned 429s until the rebalancer committed at 23:47:20. Billing ledger shows the topup succeeded later — tokens were credited back. We'll reconcile the short throttle window for the customer.

jordan-prod: This is a good catch. Two overlapping background jobs (rebalancer + topup) created a transient enforcement window. We should either make rebalancer reservations non-enforced for active requests or make topups wait for commit.

quota-bot: Action logged: INCIDENT-9903 created for "rebalance/topup race caused transient tenant quota enforcement". Assigned: oliver-sre. Priority: P2.

acme_support: Thanks — can you restore service and confirm no incorrect billing? We had ~4k requests dropped. Customer is concerned about quota being 'stolen'.

maya: Oliver, can you confirm whether credits were restored and whether to issue a goodwill topup?

oliver-sre: Credits visible again after commit at 23:47:20; enforcement lifted at ~23:47:40. I recommend a small goodwill topup for the failed requests to make the customer whole while billing reconciles — leo?

leo-billing: I'll prepare a pro-rated credit for those dropped requests and flag it as non-billable. Will follow up with acme_support in thread and update the invoice system.

jordan-prod: Longer term: adding a short-circuit in enforcer to ignore reserve flag during shard moves OR holding topups in a short retry-backoff until rebalance commit would avoid this. Filing a follow-up ticket against runtime scheduling.

maya: Follow-ups: 1) leo to issue credit (ETA 24h), 2) oliver to add metric to detect rebalance-induced enforcements (ETA 3d), 3) product to spec runbook (jordan). I'll DM acme_support with interim status and confirm when credit is applied. :white_check_mark:

acme_support: Appreciate the quick look. Please add the credit and confirm. We'll rerun the import tomorrow after you confirm the fix window.

oliver-sre: NOTE: repro steps for SRE — start a large streaming import, trigger rebalance on tenant shard, observe enforcement 429s for ~1-3 minutes. We can reproduce in staging.

maya: I'll mark this resolved for now but keep the incident open until billing and the runtime changes land. Thanks everyone. :pray:
